guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, nco_sum_q is reset to 17'h0.

When tx_enable or rx_enable is high, nco_sum_q is updated with the sum of {1'b0, nco_sum_q[NcoWidth-1:0]} and {1'b0, reg2hw.ctrl.nco.q[NcoWidth-1:0]}; the feedback uses only the lower NcoWidth bits of the previous value, ignoring higher bits.

assumptions.claim: tx_enable and rx_enable are glitch-free and valid at the clock edge when UART accumulation should proceed.
assumptions.risk: Spurious assertion causes spurious accumulation, leading to baud rate drift and potential framing or data errors.

assumptions.claim: NcoWidth matches the bit width of reg2hw.ctrl.nco.q and the intended accumulator width so that field slicing and addition do not misalign.
assumptions.risk: Mismatch could truncate or shift fields, causing incorrect fractional baud division and UART malfunction.

uncertain_points.claim: The feedback only uses nco_sum_q[NcoWidth-1:0], discarding the higher bits (including the potential carry bit at NcoWidth). It is unclear whether nco_sum_q[NcoWidth] is needed as a carry for fractional accumulation. Without seeing the rest of the module, it may be a bug that breaks baud generation.
uncertain_points.cond: When NcoWidth < 16 (since nco_sum_q is 17 bits) and the design expects a carry-out at bit NcoWidth.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect fractional accumulation leads to wrong baud rate divisor, potentially causing persistent framing errors or no communication.
